cards.title: Two gates for the sound
items: The facilitator allows Übersetzen (translate:=true, or the setup page's card); off, both workers drop what they were hearing (bridge_node.py 209–218).
The robot's phone may send sound only over this computer's own link (USB, adb reverse) or https (phone_local, wsserver.py 218–223; refused at bridge_node.py 432–437).
The guest phone needs the code from the QR code, new each time Übersetzen is allowed or the setup page asks; a new code drops the guest (bridge_node.py 233–238, wsserver.py 522–526).

cards.title: Where the words go
items: To the phones only: talk_send() writes with send_phone() and to the guest, never to a mirror, ROS, a file or the log (bridge_node.py 240–250, wsserver.py 214–217).
An error (nothing heard, no models) goes to the one who spoke only.
The phone that listens says the translation; alone, the robot's phone says it itself (talk.js 127–132).

cards.title: A letter in French
items: Reading looks for both languages while Übersetzen is allowed and counts stop words (omi.js 189–196); a German letter is read as before, with no question.
Ja sends the text in numbered pieces under the same gate as the sound (bridge_node.py 438–442); an answer with another n is dropped (omi.js 246–257).
Nein, a refusal, a failure or 20 s without an answer: the rest is read as it is, in the letter's own voice; nothing leaves the phone on Nein.
The German goes to the robot's phone only, never the guest (bridge_node.py 246); ROS gets the language found and whether it was translated, never the text (contract.py 45).

cards.title: What is kept
items: Nothing: an utterance's sound is dropped when its text is made, at most 30 s of it (translate.py 217–255).
ROS and the setup page get counts: which way, how many words, how long (bridge_node.py 270–274).
